source.name: Fact Sheet #36: Historical Deregulation Rent and Income Thresholds, FS-36 (03/2026) (NYS Homes and Community Renewal)

rules.what: All forms of deregulation of rent-stabilized apartments were repealed as of June 14, 2019, except 421-a (16) apartments. A stabilized apartment does not leave stabilization because it is vacant, no matter how long it sits empty.

Before June 14, 2019, a vacant apartment whose legal rent lawfully reached the deregulation rent threshold could leave stabilization and be rented at market rent, and an occupied apartment could be deregulated by DHCR order when both the rent and the household income reached the thresholds. In New York City the rent threshold was $2,774.76 from January 1 to June 13, 2019, and the income threshold was $200,000 from July 1, 2011 to June 13, 2019.
421-a (16) market rate apartments are the one exception to the 2019 repeal and have their own market rate threshold: $3,217.40 for 2026 ($3,123.69 in 2025, $3,040.09 in 2024).

terms.def: The pre-2019 rule that let a rent-stabilized apartment leave stabilization when it became vacant and its legal rent had reached the deregulation rent threshold. Repealed as of June 14, 2019.

The pre-2019 rule that let DHCR deregulate an occupied stabilized apartment when the rent reached the deregulation rent threshold and the household income passed the deregulation income threshold. Repealed as of June 14, 2019.

The legal rent at or above which a stabilized apartment could be deregulated before June 14, 2019. In New York City it was $2,000 from 1997, $2,500 from June 24, 2011, $2,700 from June 15, 2015, $2,733.75 in 2018 and $2,774.76 from January 1 to June 13, 2019.
